To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the following two statements are true: (1) the sufficient condition relation between a concept, fact or situation and its sufficient conditions is an epistemic process in the discovery of a scientific theory; (2) this epistemic process is a relevant logic process.

(a) a conditional is a proposition that expresses a sufficient condition relation, (b) a sufficient condition relation can be defined as a relation between a concept and its sufficient condition, (c) a concept is a proposition that describes an object or a state of affairs, (d) a sufficient condition is a proposition that can be used to infer a conclusion about the concept, (e) a sufficient condition for a concept is a sufficient condition relation of the concept, (f) a conditional is true

(a) the conditional proposition is the most general form of scientific discovery, (b) the conditional proposition can be used as the basic sentence form for a strong relevant logic model of epistemic processes in scientific discovery, (c) the conditional proposition provides an appropriate sentence form for the description of the epistemic processes of scientific discovery, and (d) a strong relevant logic can be used as a logic for the analysis and description of epistemic process in scientific discovery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two issues.

a formal model of epistemic processes of scientific discovery in which the epistemic agents (e.g., scientists) are engaged in discovering the sufficient condition relations between the concepts, facts, situations and laws in their fields of research.
a formal logic system that can describe and analyze various epistemic processes of scientific discovery.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conditional proposition is a basic sentence form used to describe various concepts, facts, situations, or conclusions in all sciences.
conditionals are the most important sentence forms in scientific research and that the study of sufficient condition relation is a central task of scientific research.
the conditional is the most fundamental and general form for scientific description and reasoning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a relevant logic model of epistemic processes in scientific discovery.
we have developed a strong relevant logic model of epistemic processes in scientific discovery.
we propose a strong relevant logic model of epistemic processes in scientific discovery.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the epistemic processes in scientific discovery are not merely about the discovery of some sufficient condition relations, but they are about the discovery of a set of sufficient condition relations that are consistent with each other.

the conditional is the most important logical form in the process of scientific discovery, because it is the only logical form that can describe the relation of the sufficient conditions between various phenomena, facts, situations and laws in scientific research.
the epistemic processes in the scientific discovery of a conditional proposition or a law can be modelled in terms of the epistemic logic of a conditional.
